name: Math — Needs & Wants (Financial Literacy)
subject: Mathematics
desc: Financial literacy lesson exploring needs vs. wants, budgeting decisions, and how personal choices affect spending. Aligned to Ontario Math curriculum.

data.lessonTitle: Needs and Wants — Making Smart Financial Decisions
data.achKnowledge: Distinguish between needs and wants with examples from daily life.
data.achThinking: Analyze spending scenarios and justify budgeting decisions using mathematical reasoning.
data.achCommunication: Clearly explain financial reasoning using vocabulary: need, want, budget, trade-off, opportunity cost.
data.achApplication: Apply understanding of needs and wants to create a simple personal budget.
data.assessDiagnostic: Think-Pair-Share: "What did you spend money on last week? Was it a need or a want?" Record responses on anchor chart.
data.assessFormative: Circulate during activity. Anecdotal notes: Can students justify their categorizations? Are they applying budget constraints?
data.assessAs: Students self-assess against success criteria checklist at end of lesson.
data.assessOf: Budget Planning Exit Ticket: students categorize 5 items and justify one trade-off decision.
data.priorLearning: Students have experience with addition and subtraction of decimals. Familiar with concept of money and making purchases.
data.differentiation:
IEP/ELL: Provide visual vocabulary cards (need vs. want with images). Simplify budget amounts to whole numbers.
Extension: research real prices online and build a monthly budget.
data.technology: Smartboard for anchor chart and scenario display. Optional: calculators for budget activity.
data.mindsOnDesc: Display image of a shopping cart full of items. Ask: "If you had $50, which of these would you buy first?" Students turn and talk. Introduce vocabulary: need, want, trade-off, budget.
data.consolidationDesc: Students share one budget decision they made and explain their trade-off. Exit ticket: categorize 3 items and explain one trade-off.
data.extension: Research the real price of 5 items from a flyer. Create a one-week budget with $100. Present: what did you choose and why?
